L8: # Near Optimal Bayesian Active Learning for Decision Making
L9: 
L10: Shervin Javdani, Yuxin Chen, Amin Karbasi, Andreas Krause, Drew Bagnell, Siddhartha Srinivasa
L11: 
L12: Proceedings of the Seventeenth International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics, PMLR 33:430-438, 2014.
L13: #### Abstract
L14: How should we gather information to make effective decisions? We address Bayesian active learning and experimental design problems, where we sequentially select tests to reduce uncertainty about a set of hypotheses. Instead of minimizing uncertainty per se, we consider a set of overlapping decision regions of these hypotheses. Our goal is to drive uncertainty into a single decision region as quickly as possible.
L15: We identify necessary and sufficient conditions for correctly identifying a decision region that contains all hypotheses consistent with observations. We develop a novel Hyperedge Cutting (HEC) algorithm for this problem, and prove that is competitive with the intractable optimal policy. Our efficient implementation of the algorithm relies on computing subsets of the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials.
L16: Finally, we demonstrate its effectiveness on two practical applications: approximate comparison-based learning and active localization using a robot manipulator.

L9: # Title:Heartbeat-Bound Hierarchical Credentials: Cryptographic Revocation for AI Agent Swarms
L10: 
L11: Authors:【5†Saurabh Deochake】
L12: 
L13: View a PDF of the paper titled Heartbeat-Bound Hierarchical Credentials: Cryptographic Revocation for AI Agent Swarms, by Saurabh Deochake

L15: 【6†View PDF】 【7†HTML (experimental)】
L16: > Abstract:Autonomous AI agents that spawn sub-agent swarms create a safety gap: existing credential revocation mechanisms, OAuth~2.0 introspection, OCSP, and W3C Status Lists, require network connectivity to a central authority, leaving ``zombie agents'' executing privileged operations for minutes to hours after operator shutdown. We present Heartbeat-Bound Hierarchical Credentials (HBHC), a cryptographic protocol that binds credential validity to periodic parent liveness proofs.
L17: Verifiers enforce freshness using only a cached public key and local clock; no network round-trip is required. When heartbeat generation ceases, all descendant credentials become unusable within a deterministically bounded window $W_z \le W_{\max} + \Delta_h + \epsilon$, conditional on bounded clock skew and parent keys held in secure enclaves.
L18: Evaluation at the protocol layer and with real LLM-backed agent swarms (GPT-4o-mini) demonstrates a 90$\times$ reduction in the zombie window over OAuth~2.0, 0.26~ms full authentication in Rust, 18,000+ verifications per second under concurrent HTTP load, and stable per-verification latency from 10 to 10,000 agents.
L19: Real-agent experiments show 0.71\% end-to-end overhead on tool calls, zero post-revocation tool calls under prompt injection that bypasses application-layer guardrails, and cascading revocation across a 49-agent four-level hierarchy within the theoretical bound.

L18: # Restoration Evidence Records for AI Agent Incident Response
L19: ## 【0†Abstract】
L20: When an AI agent system is stopped, restricted or has its credentials revoked during an incident, someone later decides whether it may run again. Incident response guidance asks for that decision to be documented with the risk that remains, but no format says what the record must contain for a party outside the deploying organization to check it.
L21: This document defines five record types for that purpose: an incident action authorization, a revocation sweep, a re-enable decision, a joint authority assignment for incidents that span organizations, and a revocation boundary report. Each is an in-toto Statement carried in a DSSE envelope, uses the canonical form of the agent audit record, and is checked by ordered rules with a named reason for each failure. A bundle rule set binds a re-enable decision to the records it cites, by digest.
L22: A published conformance corpus carries a reject member for every rule that a member can force.【1†¶】

L109: ## 【21†1.】 【22†Introduction】
L110: The agent audit record [【86†AUDIT-RECORD】] records one authorization decision and its observed effect. An incident adds decisions that record does not carry: who authorized a pause or a revocation, which credentials the revocation reached, who decided that the stopped system may resume and on what evidence, and, when two organizations are involved, which of them may act on which asset. These decisions are made over time, by different parties, and they refer to one another.
L111: The proposed charter of the AUDIT working group [【87†AUDIT-CHARTER】] names "authorization state over time" among the things its data models should represent; this document covers that state for the period from containment to restoration. Section 11 of [【88†AIMS】] likewise requires durable audit logs covering "authorization decisions and subsequent remediations" and leaves their form open; the records here give the remediation half a form.【89†¶】
